definitions.explanation: The act of secretly listening to a conversation that is not intended for you to hear.

examples.japanese: {盗|ぬす}み{聞|ぎ}きはよくない。
examples.english: Eavesdropping is not a good thing to do.

examples.japanese: {隣|となり}の{部屋|へや}の{会話|かいわ}を{盗|ぬす}み{聞|ぎ}きしてしまった。
examples.english: I accidentally overheard the conversation in the next room.

examples.japanese: {壁|かべ}に{耳|みみ}を{当|あ}てて{盗|ぬす}み{聞|ぎ}きをしているのを{見|み}つかって、ひどく{怒|おこ}られた。
examples.english: I was caught eavesdropping with my ear against the wall and got severely scolded.

notes:
A compound of {盗|ぬす}む (to steal) and {聞|き}く (to listen), with rendaku changing き to ぎ. Literally means "stealing a listen." The verb form is {盗|ぬす}み{聞|ぎ}きする.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {盗|ぬす}み{聞|ぎ}きをする: to eavesdrop
- {盗|ぬす}み{聞|ぎ}きされる: to be eavesdropped on
- {電話|でんわ}の{盗|ぬす}み{聞|ぎ}き: phone tapping

RELATED WORDS:
- {盗|ぬす}み{見|み}: peeping, peeking — the visual equivalent, secretly watching
- {盗聴|とうちょう}: wiretapping, bugging — a more technical/legal term for electronic eavesdropping
- {立|た}ち{聞|ぎ}き: overhearing while standing nearby — less intentional than {盗|ぬす}み{聞|ぎ}き
